tasks.short: Evaluate a foster or adoption applicant's home and characteristics.

steps.what: Read the foster application and the earlier checks.
Visit and notice conditions in the foster home.
Listen to the adoption applicant in the home.
Decide whether these foster home conditions are suitable.
Write the evaluation of personal characteristics and conditions.

tasks.design: She still visits the home, listens, decides whether the conditions are suitable, and writes the evaluation herself. No system scores the applicant. She writes that evaluation into the case file in {OTHER}; nothing else writes it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Suitability depends on what she sees and hears in the home, and a form cannot judge personal characteristics.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes that visit. A model that scored applicants would be an eligibility decision, and this design does not score them.
tasks.still_hard: The visit, the conversation, the suitability decision, and the written evaluation stay with her.
tasks.human_edge: She notices the home and the people in it, and she decides whether those conditions are suitable.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still visits, decides, and writes the evaluation.

reach.task: Read the home evaluation before a placement
reach.learn: Which characteristics and home conditions the placement needs from the visit

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: she observes the home and decides suitability herself. Software does not see the home or score the applicant.
GDPR article 22 bars an eligibility decision based solely on automated processing. This design does not decide suitability by automation.

EU AI Act Annex III point 5(a) covers eligibility for public assistance and services, including healthcare, by or for public authorities. Whether this employer is a public authority is unknown. This design does not score applicants.
GDPR article 9 treats health data as a special category. Personal characteristics and home conditions can include health.

assumptions: Personal characteristics and home conditions can be special-category data. She records only what this evaluation needs.
The foster application and the earlier checks are produced by the applicant and by prior checks, outside this task. Reading them is not a saving.
If the employer is a public authority, a system that scored applicants would fall under eligibility rules for public services. This design does not score them.
No audio of the visit is stored.
Zero extra hours: no system is built for this task, so there is no upkeep to count.
unknowns: Whether this employer is a public authority.
What share of the evaluation is already a fixed form.
research_questions: Which facts the placing social worker actually uses from the visit note.

incremental.description: No system is added for the home evaluation, so upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The home visit, the suitability decision, and the written evaluation stay with her. Nothing in this task is shortened. This is not a measured timing study.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Interview for the social research and file the checked summary.

steps.what: Read the question for this social research.
Interview the family for this social research.
Decide which social research findings to keep.
Write the social research notes in her words.
Draft the social research summary from those notes.

loop.input: The social worker's source notes for this inquiry, in her own words.
loop.output: A draft research summary, or a blank draft if the notes are empty.
loop.check: The social worker, in the next step, compares each finding and any risk statement with the notes. A finding or a risk sentence that is not in the notes fails.
loop.stop: One pass. If the notes are empty, or a finding is not in the notes, the draft is blank and she writes the summary herself.
loop.why_not_simpler: The notes are free text. A fixed form cannot assemble a research summary from them.

steps.what: Check the social research summary against the notes.
File the checked social research summary in the case file.

tasks.design: She still interviews the family, decides which findings to keep, and writes the source notes herself. {WORKFLOW} drafts a research summary only from those notes, then files that summary in the case file in {OTHER} only after she checks that every finding and every risk statement is in her notes. A blank note files nothing.
tasks.previous_blocker: The interview is free conversation, and a summary that adds a risk sentence she did not write would be unsafe to keep.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can restate notes she has already written, and she can refuse any finding that is not in those notes before the file step runs.
tasks.still_hard: The interview, the choice of findings, and the source notes stay with her. A short note produces a blank draft.
tasks.human_edge: She hears the family, chooses which findings to keep, and checks that every risk statement is one she wrote.
tasks.altitude: She still does the interviews. She stops retyping a summary that only restates notes she already wrote, and only when those notes exist.

reach.task: Tell the social worker the child's attendance and the concern
reach.learn: Which school facts belong in the research notes

evidence.claim: Rapportage-assistent records the Wmo or Jeugdwet intake of a Dutch municipal team and drafts the report; a worker checks every output. Pilot since May 2025, with a DPIA done. The digest names the task as maintaining case history records.
Model knowledge: she still interviews the family and writes the source notes. Free text is not a fixed form, so a draft can only restate notes she has written.

Gemeente Hengelo with Deloitte, 2024, made summaries of Wmo kitchen-table talks. No figures. The summaries were weaker on mental complaints and multiple problems than on mobility. Consultants kept their own notes, so little time was saved.
UK social workers found invented risk statements, including suicidal ideation, in notes produced by a model. One council's own check was less positive than the vendor's evaluation.
GDPR article 9 treats health data as a special category. A research summary can contain family and health words.
GDPR article 22 bars an eligibility decision based solely on automated processing. This research summary does not approve or refuse a service.

A Dutch municipal drafter claims the article 6(3) narrow procedural exception for drafting. Profiling is always high-risk. This loop drafts from notes she wrote and does not profile. Whether a child-welfare research draft is high-risk is not settled here. She checks before anything is filed.
AI literacy under article 4 applies now, and this task uses a model to draft.

assumptions: No audio of the interview is stored. A later design that recorded interviews would need works-council consent where a council exists. That time is not counted here.
The social worker writes the source notes in s4. The draft step reads only those notes. If the notes are empty, the draft is blank and the file step writes nothing.
The summary does not approve or refuse a service.
Name, family circumstances, and health words can be special-category data. Retention is for the customer and is not chosen here.
The case papers she reads at the start already exist. This task does not create them.
unknowns: What share of inquiries are already a form versus free-text notes.
research_questions: What share of her research time is the interview versus retyping a summary she has already noted.

already_counted.description: She compares each finding and any risk statement with the notes she wrote. That review time sits on the check step.

incremental.description: Keep the blank-note rule and the rule that a risk sentence must be one she wrote.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High counts only part of retyping a summary already in her notes. Interviews, the decision, and the notes stay in full. Low: the notes are too short, the draft stays blank, and she still writes the summary. This is not a published admin percentage and not a measured timing study.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise social workers and write the supervision note.

steps.what: List open cases for the social workers she supervises.
Listen to the social worker during supervision.
Decide the guidance this social worker needs.
Show the social worker the next case step.
Write the supervision note for that social worker.

tasks.design: The case file in {OTHER} lists a social worker's open cases only when worker, status and next date are already stored. She still meets the social worker, decides the guidance, shows the next step, and writes the supervision note. A blank status is left off the list and she asks in the meeting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Open cases lived in separate files, and a list of worker speed would be staff monitoring.
tasks.enabler_now: When the case worker has already stored worker, status, and next date, the case file can list those rows before the meeting.
tasks.still_hard: The meeting, the guidance decision, showing the next step, and the supervision note stay with her. A blank status is omitted.
tasks.human_edge: She listens, decides the guidance, and shows the next step in the room.
tasks.altitude: The week is still the supervision meeting. She stops opening every case only when worker, status, and next date are filled.

reach.task: Record worker, case status and next date on the case
reach.learn: Which statuses the supervision list can trust

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a case file can list rows that already hold worker, status, and next date. The supervision meeting stays with her.

Dutch works-council rules require consent before staff conversations are recorded. This design stores no audio. A list used to judge staff speed or attendance would be monitoring and would need consent where a works council exists. This list is open cases, with worker, status, and next date, not a score.
GDPR article 9 treats health data as a special category. The supervision conversation can discuss health. The list fields are worker, status, and next date only.

assumptions: The case worker records worker, case status, and next date on their own case, outside this task. That capture is not this task's time and is not counted as saved.
If worker, status, or next date is blank, that row is omitted and she asks during the meeting, which stays at full time.
The list step only reads those rows. It does not score the worker and it does not log her speed.
She writes the supervision note herself. There is no second copy step.
A small allowance keeps the three-field rule and the omit-if-blank rule.
unknowns: Whether next date is already a field the case worker fills.
Whether a works council would treat the list as performance monitoring.
research_questions: What share of supervision time is opening cases versus the meeting.

incremental.description: Keep the rule that a row needs worker, status, and next date, and that a blank field omits the row.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High is only the lookup of open cases when worker, status, and next date are filled. The meeting, the decision, showing the next step, and the note stay in full. Low: statuses are blank, so she still opens each case. This is not a performance score and not a measured timing study.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Lead the group counseling session and write the note.

steps.what: Read the group list for this counseling session.
Lead the group counseling session on grief or stress.
Decide when grief or stress needs a pause.
Tell the group the support step for this session.
Write the counseling note for grief or stress.

tasks.design: She still leads the group counseling session, notices when grief or stress needs a pause, tells the group the next step, and writes the note herself. No system speaks for her, and nothing scores the group.
tasks.previous_blocker: The session is live counselling. A note taken from a recording can add a risk sentence nobody said, and a re-offending score has failed in probation use.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new replaces the group. She still leads it and writes the note.
tasks.still_hard: Leading, noticing distress, telling the group, and the note stay with her.
tasks.human_edge: She notices when grief or stress needs a pause, and she tells the group what to do next.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still leads the group and writes the note.

reach.task: Take a referral when the group session is not enough
reach.learn: Which signs of distress she will hand over

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: leading the group, noticing distress, telling the group, and writing the note stay with her. No recording and no draft are used.
GDPR article 9 treats health data as a special category. Grief and chemical dependency can be health data.
For GGZ, the treatment dossier is kept 20 years. School and community groups may not be that treatment, so this design sets no retention period.
EU AI Act Annex III point 6(d) covers re-offending risk. This session does not score re-offending.
Inspectie JenV found a probation re-offending formula had been wrong since 2018, mostly too low, and paused it in February 2026. This session does not score risk.

assumptions: Grief and chemical dependency can be health data. She writes only the short note this session needs.
No audio is stored, and nothing scores re-offending or distress.
If this session is GGZ treatment, a long dossier retention rule may apply. School and community groups may not be that treatment. Retention is not chosen here.
The group list is produced by earlier enrollment, outside this task. She only reads it. No machine step uses it.
Zero extra hours: no system is built for this task, so there is no upkeep to count.
unknowns: Whether this session is GGZ treatment.
Whether a referral path already exists.
research_questions: Does she already write one short note per session in the case file.

incremental.description: No system is added for the group session, so upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Leading the group, noticing distress, telling the group, and writing the note stay with her. Nothing is shortened. This is not a measured timing study.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still home visits, supervision meetings, and group sessions. She stops retyping a research summary that only restates notes she wrote, and she stops opening every case for the supervision list when worker, status and next date are filled.
